title: Your Japanese is so good
setting: A weekday at the office. Emma came from abroad to join Tanaka-san's team a month ago and works next to Mai. Tanaka-san takes Mai aside to ask how Emma is getting on.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, chotto hanashi ga aru n desu kedo, ima ii desu ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん、ちょっと話があるんですけど、今いいですか？
lines.kana: きむらさん、ちょっとはなしがあるんですけど、いまいいですか？
lines.english: Kimura-san, there's something I'd like to talk to you about. Have you got a minute?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: はい、大丈夫です。何でしょう？
lines.kana: はい、だいじょうぶです。なんでしょう？
lines.english: Yes, of course. What is it?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ema-san na n desu kedo, uchi ni kite, mou ikkagetsu desu ne. dou desu ka?
lines.ja: エマさんなんですけど、うちに来て、もう一か月ですね。どうですか？
lines.kana: えまさんなんですけど、うちにきて、もういっかげつですね。どうですか？
lines.english: It's about Emma. She's been with us a month now. How's she getting on?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ema-san desu ka? sugoku shigoto ga dekiru n desu yo.
lines.ja: エマさんですか？すごく仕事ができるんですよ。
lines.kana: えまさんですか？すごくしごとができるんですよ。
lines.english: Emma? She's really good at her job.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee, atama ga ii desu kara ne.
lines.ja: ええ、頭がいいですからね。
lines.kana: ええ、あたまがいいですからね。
lines.english: Yes, well, she's a smart one.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. sore ni, fuku no sensu mo ii n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。それに、服のセンスもいいんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。それに、ふくのセンスもいいんですよ。
lines.english: She is. And she's got great taste in clothes, too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: fuku desu ka. jaa, nihongo wa dou desu ka?
lines.ja: 服ですか。じゃあ、日本語はどうですか？
lines.kana: ふくですか。じゃあ、にほんごはどうですか？
lines.english: Clothes, is it? And what about her Japanese?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: nihongo mo sugoku jouzu desu yo!
lines.ja: 日本語もすごく上手ですよ！
lines.kana: にほんごもすごくじょうずですよ！
lines.english: Her Japanese is really good too!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jibun de wa, nihongo wa sukoshi dekimasu tte itte imashita kedo ne.
lines.ja: 自分では、日本語は少しできますって言っていましたけどね。
lines.kana: じぶんでは、にほんごはすこしできますっていっていましたけどね。
lines.english: She told me herself that she speaks 'a little Japanese', though.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sukoshi ja nai desu yo! nihongo, watashi yori jouzu kamo shiremasen.
lines.ja: 少しじゃないですよ！日本語、私より上手かもしれません。
lines.kana: すこしじゃないですよ！にほんご、わたしよりじょうずかもしれません。
lines.english: That's not 'a little'! Her Japanese might be better than mine.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kinou, ema-san no hanashi mo kikimashita yo.
lines.ja: 昨日、エマさんの話も聞きましたよ。
lines.kana: きのう、えまさんのはなしもききましたよ。
lines.english: I sat down with Emma yesterday too, and heard what she had to say.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: エマさん、何て言っていましたか？
lines.kana: えまさん、なんていっていましたか？

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san wa atama ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru shi, sensu mo ii tte.
lines.ja: 木村さんは頭がいいし、仕事もできるし、センスもいいって。
lines.kana: きむらさんはあたまがいいし、しごともできるし、センスもいいって。
lines.english: That you're smart, you're great at your job, and you've got good taste.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? watashi desu ka? atama ga ii no wa ema-san desu yo!
lines.ja: え？私ですか？頭がいいのはエマさんですよ！
lines.kana: え？わたしですか？あたまがいいのはえまさんですよ！
lines.english: What? Me? Emma's the smart one!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore kara, kimura-san wa nihongo mo jouzu da tte.
lines.ja: それから、木村さんは日本語も上手だって。
lines.kana: それから、きむらさんはにほんごもじょうずだって。
lines.english: Oh, and that your Japanese is very good, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.kana: でもわたし、にほんじんですよ！

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: joudan desu yo. ema-san wa minna ni, nihongo jouzu desu ne tte iwarete imasu kara ne.
lines.ja: 冗談ですよ。エマさんはみんなに、日本語上手ですねって言われていますからね。
lines.kana: じょうだんですよ。えまさんはみんなに、にほんごじょうずですねっていわれていますからね。
lines.english: She was joking. Everyone's always telling her, 'Your Japanese is so good!'

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, ashita ema-san ni itte okimasu. iie, mada mada desu tte.
lines.ja: じゃあ、明日エマさんに言っておきます。いいえ、まだまだですって。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あしたえまさんにいっておきます。いいえ、まだまだですって。
lines.english: Then tomorrow I'll tell Emma: 'Oh no, I've still got a long way to go.'

choices.english: Mai says Emma only speaks a little Japanese, so Tanaka-san asks Mai to help her with it.
Mai praises Emma, and Tanaka-san tells her Emma said the same kind of things about Mai, even joking that Mai's Japanese is good.
Emma told Tanaka-san that Mai's Japanese is hard to follow, so Mai plans to speak to her more simply tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Tanaka-san asks how Emma is doing after her first month. In lines 4-10 Mai praises her: she's great at her job (shigoto ga dekiru), she has good taste in clothes (fuku no sensu mo ii), and her Japanese may even be better than Mai's (line 10). Line 11: Tanaka-san talked with Emma yesterday too, and line 13 gives what Emma said about Mai: atama ga ii, shigoto mo dekiru, sensu mo ii. In line 15 Emma also said Mai's Japanese is good, and line 17 explains it was a joke, because everyone says that to Emma. A is wrong: Emma is the one who says she speaks 'a little' (line 9), Mai says that isn't true (line 10), and nobody asks Mai to help. C is wrong: Emma praised Mai's Japanese as a joke. She didn't complain about it, and tomorrow Mai will joke back with iie, mada mada desu (line 18).

questions.english: Mai tells Tanaka-san that Emma is really good at her job. How does he agree?
questions.ja: 田中さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Yes, her head is skilful, after all.
choices.romaji: ee, atama ga jouzu desu kara ne.
ee, atama ga ii desu kara ne.

questions.explanation: Line 5: 'ee, atama ga ii desu kara ne.' Being smart is atama (head) with ii (good), and in casual speech ga drops (atama ii). The same pair comes back when Tanaka-san passes on what Emma said about Mai (line 13: atama ga ii shi) and when Mai answers (line 14: atama ga ii no wa ema-san desu yo). A is wrong: sumaato is the trap. In Japanese it means slim or sleek, so it would sound like a comment on Emma's figure. B is wrong: jouzu praises a skill done well, like the Japanese in lines 8 and 10 (nihongo mo sugoku jouzu). Being clever isn't a skill, so atama takes ii, never jouzu.

questions.english: Kenta has heard about your new coworker Emma and asks, "ema-san tte, nihongo dekiru no?" (Can Emma speak Japanese?) She speaks it really well. Tell him.
questions.ja: エマさんって、日本語できるの？
questions.kana: えまさんって、にほんごできるの？
questions.answer: Go beyond dekiru and praise how well she speaks, with nihongo and jouzu. Kenta is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually: un, nihongo sugoku jouzu da yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, nihongo sugoku jouzu da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、日本語すごく上手だよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, her Japanese is really good.

modelAnswers.romaji: dekiru yo! nihongo, honto ni jouzu na n da.
modelAnswers.ja: できるよ！日本語、ほんとに上手なんだ。
modelAnswers.english: She sure can! Her Japanese is really good.

questions.explanation: Kenta asks with dekiru, which only says whether someone can speak it. Jouzu says she speaks it well, and that's what you want to tell him. Mai takes the same step in lines 9-10: Emma describes herself modestly with dekiru (nihongo wa sukoshi dekimasu, 'I speak a little'), and Mai corrects that to jouzu (sukoshi ja nai desu yo! nihongo, watashi yori jouzu kamo shiremasen). Jouzu is for praising someone else's skill, so it fits when you're talking about Emma. About your own Japanese you'd say sukoshi dekimasu, or mada mada desu when someone compliments you, which is the reply Mai jokes she'll give in line 18. Among friends, nihongo umai is also fine.

questions.english: Tanaka-san asks how Emma is getting on, and Mai says, "ema-san desu ka? sugoku shigoto ga dekiru n desu yo." What does Mai mean?
questions.ja: エマさんはどうですか？
questions.kana: えまさんはどうですか？

choices.english: Emma is very capable: she's really good at her job.
Emma has a lot of work at the moment and is very busy.
Emma can now do the work by herself, without anyone's help.

questions.explanation: Line 4: shigoto ga dekiru is praise for a capable person, someone who is good at their job. Tanaka-san agrees that she's smart (line 5), and in line 13 Emma says the same about Mai (shigoto mo dekiru). It takes dekiru, not jouzu: jouzu praises a skill done well (nihongo ga jouzu), while shigoto ga dekiru says someone is capable. B is wrong: busy with work is shigoto ga isogashii, and nobody says Emma is busy. C is wrong: Mai isn't saying Emma can finally manage alone (that would be hitori de dekiru). She's praising how good Emma is at her job.

questions.english: Yuki holds up a new outfit: "mite mite! kinou, kaimono ni itte kita n da. kono fuku, dou?" (Look! I went shopping yesterday. What do you think of this?) You love it. Compliment her taste.
questions.ja: 見て見て！昨日、買い物に行ってきたんだ。この服、どう？
questions.kana: みてみて！きのう、かいものにいってきたんだ。このふく、どう？
questions.romaji: mite mite! kinou, kaimono ni itte kita n da. kono fuku, dou?
questions.answer: Praise her taste with sensu and ii. Yuki is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually: sensu ii ne!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugoku ii! sensu ii ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すごくいい！センスいいね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's great! You've got good taste.

modelAnswers.romaji: yuki tte, honto ni sensu ii yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ユキって、ほんとにセンスいいよね。
modelAnswers.english: You've really got great taste, Yuki.

questions.explanation: Taste in clothes is sensu with ii. Mai uses it about Emma in line 6 (fuku no sensu mo ii n desu yo), and Emma uses it about Mai in line 13 (sensu mo ii). Don't reach for aji: that's taste as in flavour. Also watch the false friend: sensu nai means 'no taste', not 'that doesn't make sense'. Yuki is talking casually, so drop ga; to Tanaka-san it would be sensu ga ii desu ne.

newWords.english: how, how about (dou desu ka? = how is she doing? / what do you think?)
clothes (fuku no sensu = taste in clothes)
say (itte imashita = said; iwarete imasu = gets told; itte okimasu = I'll tell her)
a joke (joudan desu yo = (she's) only joking)
